title: Delegated-Authority Conformance Vector (ERDL-anchored)
description: One delegated-authority conformance vector. The verdict is produced by the ERDL expression engine (erdl-landing) evaluating the vector's rule over its scenario context — per DESIGN.md §8a, not a hand-written state machine. Each vector carries an ERDL rule (when constraint-comparison → then DENY), an attack context (violating), a legal context (non-violating baseline), and the expected attribution.

profile.description: stateless = no revocation/freshness; stateful = AV-05/AV-10 later

rule.description: The ERDL rule (RuleDefinition) whose when-condition is the constraint comparison and whose then-action is the conforming decision. The rule id encodes the invariant.

id.description: Rule id; the invariant is the prefix (e.g. INV-01_...)

attack.description: The violating scenario context (fields the rule's condition reads).

legal.description: A non-violating context (positive baseline; blocks a deny-all implementation).

attribution.description: Scenario attribution (public; per Annam §10 attributable rejection). Engine-derived fields (decision/matched_invariant) are NOT here — they live in the answer oracle.

violation_hop.description: first hop where the authority transition became invalid (= first_invalid_boundary)

requested_action.description: the protected effect requested, e.g. write(Resource-R)

effective_authority.description: the effective task authority, e.g. read(Resource-R)
